description: Canonical controlled vocabulary for technical context dimensions used by A.R.I.A. Context describes the circumstances under which technical information, evidence, knowledge, experience, relationships, hypotheses, actions, and reasoning are applicable. Context dimensions classify contextual meaning; they do not duplicate canonical entities or create a parallel technical ontology.

principles: Context describes technical applicability and circumstances; it does not replace the object being contextualized.
Canonical technical objects shall be referenced by canonical identity rather than recreated as context-specific duplicates.
A context dimension identifies what kind of contextual information is being represented.
A contextual value supplies the applicable value or canonical reference for that dimension.
Unknown context is a valid state.
Missing context shall only be requested when it is expected to materially improve technical reasoning.
Context similarity is multidimensional and shall not be reduced to simple equality unless technically justified.
Different context dimensions may have different importance for different technical questions.
Historical context shall be preserved when later context changes.
Context does not establish source authority.
Context match does not establish causal truth.

value_model.principle: A context dimension may be represented by a canonical entity reference, structured value, measurement reference, controlled scalar, free technical value, or explicitly unknown state depending on the dimension.

value_kinds.description: References an existing canonical A.R.I.A. object by its canonical runtime identifier.
Represents contextual information requiring a structured value that is not itself a reusable canonical entity.
References a measurement record when a measured technical condition provides context.
Uses a controlled value defined by the applicable authoritative Registry or schema.
Stores a bounded technical value when canonicalization would not provide meaningful reuse.
Explicitly represents that the applicable contextual value is not currently known.
Explicitly represents that the context dimension does not apply to the technical object or question.

rules: CANONICAL_REFERENCE is preferred when the contextual value already exists as a reusable canonical object.
A Registry-definition code shall not be substituted for runtime canonical identity when a runtime object reference is required.
Unknown and not-applicable are distinct.
Absence of a value shall not automatically be interpreted as unknown, false, or not applicable.
Measurements used as context retain their measurement identity and provenance.

dimensions.description: Identifies the manufacturer materially applicable to the technical object, system, evidence, knowledge, experience, or reasoning operation.
examples: manufacturer of the equipment under diagnosis
manufacturer whose documentation is being evaluated
rules: The manufacturer shall be referenced rather than recreated inside the context record.
Manufacturer match alone does not establish product applicability.

dimensions.description: Identifies the applicable reusable product family when product-family context materially affects technical reasoning.
rules: Product-family context shall not replace more specific product or variant context when those distinctions materially affect applicability.

dimensions.description: Identifies the specific canonical product materially applicable to the technical context.
rules: Product identity shall remain canonical and reusable outside the case.
A product name shall not be used as identity when a canonical product reference exists.

dimensions.description: Identifies the applicable product variant, model variant, hardware variant, or other canonical product specialization when technically material.
rules: Variant context shall be preserved when technical behavior, compatibility, procedure, limits, or documentation differ by variant.

dimensions.description: Identifies the hardware revision or hardware-generation context when revision differences materially affect technical applicability.
rules: A hardware revision may remain a technical value unless it becomes sufficiently reusable to justify canonical representation.
Revision applicability shall not be inferred solely from product name.

dimensions.description: Identifies software, application, operating-system, controller, or management-system version context when technically material.
rules: Version ranges and exact versions shall remain distinguishable.
Software applicability may be temporal.

dimensions.description: Identifies firmware or embedded software version context when firmware materially affects technical behavior, configuration, compatibility, or procedure.
Represents technically material configuration state affecting expected behavior, compatibility, diagnosis, or applicability.
rules: Configuration context should reference canonical configuration entities when such entities exist.
Large configuration payloads should remain source artifacts or structured configuration records rather than being duplicated into context.
Only technically material configuration dimensions should be projected into reasoning context.

dimensions.description: Represents the technically relevant arrangement, connectivity, path, interface relationships, or system topology applicable to the technical question.
rules: Topology context may reference canonical topology entities where available.
Topology should preserve directionality and endpoint distinctions when technically material.

dimensions.description: Identifies the physical, electrical, optical, radio, logical, software, or protocol interface materially involved in the technical condition.
rules: Interface context should reference a canonical interface entity when one exists.
Interface names alone shall not be assumed globally unique.

dimensions.description: Identifies a canonical component or technical element materially relevant to the technical question.
rules: Case-specific observation history shall not be embedded into the canonical component entity.

dimensions.description: Identifies the canonical technical scope applicable to the case, evidence, experience, knowledge, action, or reasoning operation.
rules: Scope describes the technical work or responsibility boundary relevant to reasoning.
Scope context shall not turn A.R.I.A. into a general project-management system.

dimensions.description: Identifies the physical or logical site relevant to technical applicability when site-specific conditions materially affect reasoning.
rules: Site identity may be represented as a generic canonical entity unless a dedicated runtime identity is later established.
Site context should only be included when technically relevant.

dimensions.description: Represents technically material geographic, structural, equipment-position, path-position, or other location information.
rules: Precise location shall only be retained when technically required.
Location and site are distinct: a site may contain multiple technically meaningful locations.

dimensions.description: Identifies the radio-frequency band or spectrum context when frequency materially affects design, behavior, propagation, interference, compatibility, or diagnosis.
rules: Frequency band context may be represented by bounded frequency values and canonical units.
Frequency band shall not be inferred from manufacturer alone.

dimensions.description: Identifies the applicable channel, channel pair, center frequency, bandwidth allocation, or equivalent channelization context.
Identifies applicable polarization context when polarization affects RF behavior, configuration, interference, alignment, or expected performance.
Identifies modulation or adaptive-modulation context when it materially affects performance, capacity, thresholds, or diagnosis.
Represents configured or expected capacity, throughput profile, channel width, traffic profile, or related performance configuration when technically relevant.
Represents technically relevant load or traffic conditions present when behavior was observed or evaluated.
rules: Traffic state should preserve observation time when behavior is time-dependent.

dimensions.description: Represents the technically relevant operational mode or equipment state under which information applies.
rules: Operating state shall not be confused with case lifecycle status.

dimensions.description: Represents environmental conditions that may materially affect technical behavior, measurements, propagation, equipment performance, or applicability.
rules: Measured environmental quantities should reference measurement records when available.
Environmental correlation does not independently establish causality.

dimensions.description: Represents relevant electrical power conditions under which technical behavior was observed or evaluated.
rules: Measured voltage, current, power, or related quantities should reference measurement records when available.

dimensions.description: Represents technically relevant grounding, bonding, shielding, or electrical-reference conditions.
Represents Ethernet, IP, VLAN, routing, switching, timing, synchronization, or other transport conditions materially affecting technical reasoning.
Identifies the technically relevant communications, management, signaling, synchronization, or application protocol context.
Represents the relevant alarm state or alarm combination present during a technical observation or reasoning operation.
rules: An alarm may also be persisted as evidence; contextual projection shall not duplicate or replace the evidence record.
Alarm presence does not independently establish root cause.

dimensions.description: References canonical symptom entities materially relevant to contextual applicability or comparison.
rules: This dimension references canonical symptoms; it does not define symptom vocabulary.
Symptoms remain distinct from failure modes and causes.

dimensions.description: References a canonical failure mode when historical experience, knowledge, validation, or other technical information is explicitly contextualized to that failure mode.
rules: Failure-mode context shall not be used to assert that the failure mode is present in the current case.
Current case evaluation of a failure mode belongs in hypothesis and evidence reasoning.

dimensions.description: References or represents technically relevant conditions under which measurements were obtained, compared, or interpreted.
rules: Actual measured values retain meas_<UUID> identity.
Units remain governed by the applicable unit Registry.
Measurement context shall preserve method and conditions when they materially affect interpretation.

dimensions.description: Identifies the canonical tool, instrument, tester, software utility, or technical apparatus materially relevant to evidence quality, measurement interpretation, or procedure applicability.
rules: Tool identity shall not substitute for calibration or measurement-confidence information.

dimensions.description: Identifies a technically relevant procedure, method, test process, or workflow under which evidence, actions, or outcomes were produced.
rules: Procedure applicability may depend on manufacturer, product, revision, configuration, and safety context.

dimensions.description: Represents safety conditions or constraints that materially affect permissible diagnostic or corrective actions.
rules: Safety constraints may prohibit otherwise diagnostically valuable actions.
A.R.I.A. shall not treat diagnostic utility as overriding applicable safety requirements.

dimensions.description: Represents physical, logical, credential, equipment, site, maintenance-window, or other access limitations materially affecting technical execution.
Represents limitations on actions due to expected or permissible impact to live service, traffic, availability, or operational continuity.
References customer-specific technical requirements, standards, acceptance criteria, configurations, or scope distinctions only when they materially affect technical reasoning.
rules: Customer context exists only to support A.R.I.A.'s technical mission.
This dimension shall not create CRM, sales, billing, or general customer-management behavior.
Reusable technical requirements should be canonicalized separately when appropriate.

dimensions.description: Represents validated team-specific technical experience, capability, procedure, or execution context when materially relevant to diagnosis or learning.
rules: Team context shall not become an employee performance or HR assessment.
Historical team patterns require sufficient validation before influencing reasoning.

dimensions.description: References technically relevant user-specific experience, capability, role, observation history, or procedural context when appropriate.
rules: User identity does not establish fault.
User-specific history may influence reasoning only when validated and contextually relevant.
A.R.I.A. shall not evolve into an HR performance system.

dimensions.description: Represents the time, interval, sequence, duration, recurrence pattern, validity period, or temporal relationship materially affecting technical interpretation or applicability.
rules: Observed time and recorded time remain distinct.
Temporal context shall not be inferred solely from record creation time.
Historical applicability shall be preserved when technical conditions later change.

dimensions.description: Represents technically relevant recent or historical changes, maintenance activity, replacements, upgrades, configuration modifications, or interventions.
rules: Temporal proximity to a change may increase diagnostic relevance but does not independently establish causality.
Change history should reference underlying events, actions, sources, or evidence when available.

dimensions.description: Represents technically relevant prior behavior, recurrence, stability, degradation, intermittent behavior, or known-good history.
rules: Historical behavior shall preserve source and temporal provenance.
Historical frequency informs priors but does not independently establish current cause.

dimensions.description: Represents the technical conditions, acceptance criteria, comparison basis, test boundaries, and other circumstances under which validation results apply.
rules: Validation context shall preserve conditions necessary to interpret whether a result generalizes beyond the specific validation event.

dimensions.description: Represents the context dimensions required to determine whether a historical Experience Ledger record is sufficiently comparable to influence current reasoning.
rules: Experience applicability is multidimensional.
Historical cases shall not be treated as equivalent merely because they share one manufacturer, symptom, product, or failure mode.
Context-match confidence remains separate from historical frequency.

dimensions.description: Represents the context boundaries under which reusable canonical technical knowledge is known or expected to apply.
rules: Canonical knowledge may be reusable without being universally applicable.
Applicability restrictions shall remain explicit rather than being hidden in prose when materially important.

dimension_categories.description: Manufacturer, product family, product, and product-variant applicability.
Hardware, software, firmware, and revision applicability.
Configuration, topology, interface, component, and operating-state context.
Site and technically relevant location context.
Frequency, channel, polarization, modulation, and other radio-specific context.
Capacity, traffic, loading, and performance-operating context.
Environmental conditions materially affecting technical behavior.
Power, grounding, bonding, shielding, and related electrical conditions.
Transport, protocol, addressing, switching, routing, timing, and related network context.
Alarm and symptom context relevant to observations.
Diagnostic contextual references that do not themselves establish current diagnosis.
Measurement conditions, instruments, and test circumstances.
Technical procedure and method context.
Technical scope, safety, access, and service-impact constraints.
Organization-specific information retained solely when materially relevant to technical reasoning.
User or team context retained solely when technically relevant.
Time, sequence, change history, recurrence, and historical behavior.
Conditions and boundaries under which validation results apply.
Context required to evaluate applicability of validated historical experience.
Applicability boundaries for reusable canonical technical knowledge.

comparison_semantics.principle: Context comparison determines technical applicability or similarity. It is not a generic object-equality test.

comparison_states.description: The compared contextual values are materially equivalent for the technical question.
The values differ but remain technically compatible for the applicable reasoning purpose.
Some technically meaningful overlap exists, but material differences remain.
A material contextual difference reduces or prevents applicability.
Available information is insufficient to determine contextual similarity.
The dimension is not relevant to the comparison being performed.

rules: Different dimensions may use different comparison methods.
Exact equality shall not be required when technically valid ranges or compatible variants exist.
A mismatch in a critical dimension may outweigh matches in several noncritical dimensions.
Unknown comparison state shall not automatically be treated as mismatch.
Context similarity methods are owned by the Context Engine, not this Registry.
The comparison result may contribute to CONTEXT_MATCH_CONFIDENCE but is not itself confidence.

states.description: The available context is sufficient for the current technical reasoning operation.
Some material context is missing, but useful reasoning remains possible.
Missing context materially prevents a defensible reasoning operation.
A.R.I.A. cannot yet determine whether the available context is sufficient.

rules: Context completeness is relative to the technical question.
A context record does not need every Registry dimension populated.
A.R.I.A. should request additional context only when expected information value justifies doing so.
Missing nonmaterial context shall not unnecessarily block reasoning.
Context completeness is not a confidence dimension by itself, although it may influence confidence.

applicability_rules.rule: Context dimensions shall not duplicate canonical entity definitions.
When a reusable canonical object exists, context shall reference its canonical runtime identifier rather than recreate it.
Manufacturer context does not establish product, variant, revision, configuration, or temporal applicability.
Product context does not establish revision or configuration applicability when those distinctions are technically material.
Failure-mode context does not assert that a failure mode is present in the current case.
Symptom context does not establish cause.
Measurements used as contextual information retain measurement identity, units, provenance, and measurement confidence.
Context-match confidence and hypothesis probability remain separate.
Context similarity and source authority remain separate.
Historical experience shall be weighted according to technically material contextual similarity rather than superficial record similarity.
Unknown context shall remain representable and shall not be silently filled by model inference.
Model-inferred context shall remain distinguishable from observed, supplied, retrieved, or validated context.
Temporal applicability shall be evaluated when product revisions, software, firmware, procedures, standards, configuration, or known behavior changes over time.
Context changes shall not silently rewrite the historical context under which prior evidence, actions, outcomes, or experience occurred.
Context used to retrieve Knowledge Graph information shall respect any applicability boundaries attached to that knowledge.
Customer, team, and user context may be represented only where it materially supports A.R.I.A.'s technical mission.
Context shall not become a substitute for CRM, HR, accounting, sales, or general project-management data.
Context comparison methods shall preserve dimension-specific significance and shall not assume that all dimensions contribute equally.
A context record may contain references to multiple values for a dimension when the technical situation legitimately involves multiple applicable objects.
Contradictory contextual information shall be preserved and reconciled rather than silently overwritten.

provenance_semantics.principle: Material context should retain enough provenance to distinguish supplied, observed, measured, retrieved, derived, and inferred contextual information.
rules: Origin type does not replace the Core provenance contract.
MODEL_INFERRED context requires structured acceptance before becoming authoritative persisted context.
Derived context should retain lineage to its parent information.
A canonical reference does not eliminate the need to preserve how A.R.I.A. determined that the reference was applicable to the current context.

context_engine_role: calculates or contributes to context-match confidence
determines which context dimensions are material to a technical question
orchestration_engine_role: determines when context resolution or re-resolution is required
rules: This Registry shall not implement context similarity algorithms.
This Registry shall not determine retrieval ranking.
This Registry shall not calculate hypothesis probability.
This Registry shall not persist authoritative case state.

prohibited_uses: Creating duplicate manufacturers inside context records.
Creating duplicate products inside context records.
Creating duplicate product variants inside context records.
Creating duplicate symptoms inside context records.
Creating duplicate failure modes inside context records.
Creating duplicate measurements inside context records.
Using Registry-definition codes as runtime canonical object identifiers.
Treating context match as source authority.
Treating context match as hypothesis probability.
Treating symptom context as causal proof.
Treating failure-mode context as confirmation that the failure mode exists in the current case.
Treating missing context as negative evidence unless the absence itself is technically meaningful.
Silently replacing historical context with current context.
Persisting model-inferred context as authoritative without structured acceptance.
Using customer context for CRM behavior.
Using user or team context for HR performance assessment.
Embedding large source artifacts or configuration exports directly into context when references are sufficient.
Using this Registry to define reasoning-state or lifecycle-state vocabulary.
